text:
Iaccuci c. Succession d’Occhionero

2018 QCCS 319

SUPERIOR COURT

CANADA

PROVINCE OF QUEBEC

DISTRICT OF

MONTREAL

N° :

500-17-086529-156

DATE :

February 2, 2018

______________________________________________________________________

IN THE
PRESENCE OF :

THE
HONOURABLE

MARIE-CLAUDE
ARMSTRONG, s.c.j.

______________________________________________________________________

FRANCESCA IACCUCI

and

GIANNI OCCHIONERO

and

LISA OCCHIONERO

Applicants

vs.

THE HEIRS OF THE ESTATE OF THE
LATE ALDO OCCHIONERO

and

RINA OCCHIONERO

Defendants

and

Mtre. CLAUDE CHARTRAND
,

Impleaded party

______________________________________________________________________

JUDGMENT

______________________________________________________________________

1.

INTRODUCTION AND CONTEXT

[
1
]

On May 2, 2014, Aldo Occhionero (“
Aldo
”)
[1]
died of stomach cancer.  He
was 76 years old. Married to Francesca Iaccuci (“
Francesca
”) since 1972,
the couple had two children, Gianni Occhionero (“
Gianni
”) and Lisa
Occhionero (“
Lisa
”).

[
2
]

A few months before his death, on February 25, 2014, Aldo signed a
Last Will and Testament (the “
Will
”) before Mtre. Claude Chartrand, notary
and impleaded party.  Apart from this Will, Aldo left no other previous will or
testamentary provisions.

[
3
]

Under the terms of the Will, Aldo’s sister, Rina Occhionero (“
Rina
”),
is the sole heir and beneficiary of the Aldo’s estate, as well as its
liquidator.

[
4
]

Aldo had been living with his sister Rina for a few weeks when he
signed the Will.

[
5
]

Francesca, Gianni and Lisa ask the Court to declare the Will null
and void on the ground that Aldo was subject to Rina’s undue influence and/or
that he lacked sufficient capacity to make a Will in February 2014.

[
6
]

Francesca also asks the Court to appoint her liquidator to the estate.
Gianni and Lisa are in agreement with this request.

[
7
]

As Aldo did not make any prior testament to the Will in question, if
the latter is annulled, his two children will be entitled to two thirds (2/3)
of his Estate, and his wife, to one third (1/3) and this, as per the rules of
legal devolution of successions in the
Civil Code of Quebec
.
[2]

[
8
]

Rina contests the action in nullity of the Will.  She argues that the
Will represented Aldo’s true and genuine testamentary wishes, expressed in full
capacity, free of any interference or undue influence.

[
9
]

In November 2014, in a separate file, Francesca instituted a demand
for the partition of the family patrimony.
[3]

The Court is not seized of this latter demand.  It has been suspended pending
the decision in the case at bar.

2.

RELEVANT FACTS

2.1 The Fall of 2013

[
10
]

As of September 2013, Aldo started showing
unusual behavior in and around the house he shared with Francesca.

[
11
]

Many events and incidents reported by Francesca
and Gianni indicate that Aldo’s general health and mental condition
deteriorated in 2013 and 2014.  These situations are confirmed in part by Mrs.
Line Vidal, who works as a domestic aid at Gianni’s home once every two weeks.

[
12
]

Mrs. Vidal testified that she would see Aldo two
or three times per month when performing her work at Gianni’s house, who lives
next door to his parents.  She last saw Aldo on two occasions in January 2014.
She testified that he was confused and disorganised to a point that, had he been
under her care, she would not have let him go outside alone.  She shared her
concerns about Aldo with Francesca at the time.

[
13
]

Regarding Aldo’s behavior as of September 2013,
the proof
[4]

revealed that Aldo:

-

Hit on Mrs. Line Vidal,
or attempted to scare her;

-

Was disorganised and
disoriented, attempted to hide behind cars and trees or the couch at home; some
of these situations were reported to Gianni not only by Line Vidal, but also by
neighbors;

-

Thought he was followed
when walking outside;

-

Did not respond when
questioned or offered help, would easily be distracted or incoherent in his
speech
[5]
;

-

Showed an abnormal
gait, walking with his legs widely spread apart;

-

Complained about ear
pain or sensation of water in his ear, banged his ear and even attempted to
take care of the matter himself by introducing a steak knife in his ear;

-

Blamed Francesca for his
ear problem “because she made him take showers”;

-

Was verbally
aggressive, even to his grandson Gianluca in late 2013.  From then on,
Francesca made sure Gianluca was never left alone in Aldo’s presence;

-

Was not able to carry a
normal conversation, would stare or fidget and answer with one or two words
sentences, in a whispering tone;
[6]

-

Curled up in the shower
or the bathtub, shutting the curtains to hide;

-

Barricaded himself in
the room which he used as his bedroom in the house, placing a broom between the
door handle and the wall to block the door;

-

Often cried and
complained of being tired of living;

-

Attempted to drink bleach
on February 2, 2014;

-

Cut out a bed sheet in
tiny squares and fabricated small pouches out of them, in which he put garlic
or salt, and suspended them above his bed and in his window, telling Francesca
it was to protect him from some kind of “evil”;

-

Had his day and night
activities mixed up (starting November-December 2013);

-

Peed a few times in
corners of the living room when awake at night, without showing any sense that
this was inappropriate;

-

Refused to eat the
meals Francesca prepared to him if she was present at the table;

-

Refused to have his
clothes washed, was always wearing the same pieces of clothing;

-

Refused to consult a
doctor or be brought to the hospital (or made it very difficult to accept to
attend appointments).  Aldo questioned the competence of the physicians who
would treat him, and indicated to his wife he would prefer to see doctors
recommended by his sister Rina.  He would become verbally abusive with
Francesca when she was trying to convince him to see a doctor, to the point
that he even bit her and grabbed her by the hair.  However, Also did end up consulting
doctors on his own a few times in the Fall of 2013, after being encouraged to do
so by Francesca;

-

When in anger, threw
away Francesca’s portable phone on two occasions, one of these being when she
wanted to call 911 when Aldo had vomited at a family gathering in the Iaccuci
family for New Year’s Eve.  Aldo shouted he was not sick, but Gianni came over
at Francesca’s request to calm Aldo down;

-

Tried to remove a
callus from his foot with a razor, hurt himself and bled profusely.  He refused
to be taken to the emergency room to be treated.

2.2  The period starting January 2014

[
14
]

On January 6, 2014, Aldo asked Francesca to make
an appointment at the Jewish General Hospital for his ear problem.  As a
referral was needed, Francesca suggested that he consult with his family
doctor.  Aldo objected, arguing that because he was a “noble man”, he would not
see any doctor who was not of “blue blood”.

[
15
]

Francesca discussed this with Rina who told her
she would take care of making an appointment for Aldo with a “good” doctor.

[
16
]

In about mid-January, Aldo started visiting Rina
at her house during the day, and returned home around supper time.

[
17
]

On the morning of February 2, Aldo asked
Francesca to bake a cake for Rina. Francesca obliged, and Aldo poured the
ingredients measured by Francesca in the cake mixture.   Shortly after, Aldo
started rocking in a chair, while banging his head on the back of the chair.
He complained to Francesca, saying something like “
They made me sign papers
– help me !”
.

Francesca thought Aldo was referring to the sale of
his garage to his nephews Nicholas and Angelo Xydis, who are Rina’s sons.

[
18
]

That same morning, according to Francesca, Aldo
told her “
You’re the best thing that ever happened to me

!
“; “
I
should never have listened to Rina
”.

[
19
]

Aldo visited Rina that day and brought her the
cake.  He also visited Rina on the next day (February 3), but this time, he did
not return home.

[
20
]

On February 3, Rina called Francesca to tell her
Aldo would stay with her for a few days, that she would cook for him and he
would rest.  Rina asked Francesca for Aldo’s passport to take him to her condo
in Florida.  Francesca answered that she did not know where Aldo’s passport
could be found, as he used to keep it in the safe at his garage.

[
21
]

Between February 3 and 18, Rina called Francesca
a couple of times and told her Aldo was gaining weight, was less stressed,
slept better and that he could not be disturbed.

[
22
]

However, Rina did not disclose to Francesca that
Aldo had been hospitalized at the Centre Hospitalier de Verdun (“
CH Verdun
”)
from February 5 to 14, and that he had received a diagnosis of terminal stage
stomach cancer.

[
23
]

Rina said that she did not inform Francesca out
of respect for Aldo’s specific wishes that his hospitalization and diagnosis remained
undisclosed to his wife and children.

[
24
]

Meanwhile, during the second week of February, Francesca
started calling various hospitals to enquire about Aldo.  She obtained some
information when she called at the CH Verdun.  On February 17, she was told that
Dr Evelyne Gaillardetz was scheduled to make a first home visit to Aldo that
day.

[
25
]

On February 18, Francesca tried to contact Dr
Gaillardetz, but her secretary refused to transfer the call to the doctor,
saying that they did not want to deal with “their family problems”.  Francesca,
as advised by the secretary, contacted the nurse and left a message.  Her call
was not returned.

[
26
]

On the same day, Francesca called Rina and found
out that Rina never obtained the medical referral she had undertaken to obtain
for Aldo. According to Francesca, Rina threatened her during that
conversation.  Rina warned her by saying: ”
Don’t take it to the next level,
my family will destroy yours

!
”.  Rina would also have accused
Francesca of having an affair, and mentioned that Lisa was using and selling
drugs.

[
27
]

Following that call with Rina, Francesca went to
the police station.  She was told that the police would not intervene because
the situation did not constitute a criminal matter.

[
28
]

After this, Rina only answered one of
Francesca’s phone calls.  Rina told Francesca that Aldo “
was doing fine
”.
Francesca was not able to speak to Aldo again.

2.3 Aldo’s medical file

[
29
]

Aldo’s medical file for his hospitalization at
CH Verdun (February 5 to 14, 2014) reveal the following.

-

Aldo was initially in a feverish and confused
state.
[7]

-

He was not oriented with respect to space, time
and persons on February 5.
[8]

-

Once more stable, and although considered alert on
February 12, it remained difficult for him to understand instructions, even
when given in Italian.
[9]

-

On February 11, he was not oriented with respect
to space, time and persons.
[10]

He required complete assistance to get dressed.
[11]

-

On February 13, it is noted that his gait is
polygonal with a somewhat rigid balancing of the arms.
[12]
On the day of his release
(February 14), it is noted that Aldo was feeling well, was not in pain, and was
smiling.

[
30
]

Upon his release from the hospital, it was
decided he would receive palliative care at home.

[
31
]

The notes of the physician (Dr Gallairdetz) and
of the nurse (Mrs. Valérie Caty) for the palliative care home visits from
February 17 to May 2, indicate that in general, Aldo was in a good state, with
improving spirits, that he had stopped crying, was alert, well oriented
although confused at times, and answered questions appropriately.  He was noted
to be an asymptomatic patient.
[13]

2.4 The circumstances of the signing of the Will

[
32
]

On February 23, 2014, Mtre. Claude Chartrand,
notary, was contacted by Rina’s son, Nicholas Xydis.  The latter asked the
notary to call Aldo for the making of a will.  Mtre. Chartrand communicated with
Aldo at Rina’s house.  Aldo told him on the phone that he wanted to make a will
in which he would leave everything to his sister Rina.  Notary Chartrand indicated
he would prepare the Will and visit Aldo on February 25 to have it signed.

[
33
]

On February 25, as planned, Mtre. Chartrand
arrived at Rina’s house.  She opened the door and showed Mtre. Chartrand to the
kitchen, where Aldo was already seated at the kitchen table.  The meeting
between Mtre. Chartrand and Aldo lasted 10 to 15 minutes, while Rina and the
son of Mtre. Chartrand (whom he had taken with him to act as second witness to
the Will), waited in another room.  According to notary Chartrand’s testimony,
his impression of Aldo was that he was “well” and that his condition did not
raise any concern for the signing of a Will.

2.5 The events after the signing of the Will

[
34
]

On March 12, Francesca was served with a letter
signed by a lawyer acting on behalf of Aldo.

[
35
]

The letter mentioned that Francesca refused to
care for him and wanted him to move in with his sister Rina.  The lawyer
alleged that Francesca frequently called to speak to Aldo, even though he did
not want any further contact with her, because his health condition required peace
and calm.  Francesca was thus formally required to stop communicating with
Aldo. The letter concluded by mentioning that Francesca’s attempts constituted
harassment and that any further attempt she would make to contact him would be
followed by legal procedures.
[14]

[
36
]

Aldo passed away on May 2 at Rina’s house.  Francesca,
Lisa and Gianni were not informed of his death.

3.

THE ISSUES BEFORE THE COURT

[
37
]

The Court must decide of the following issues:

a)

Did Aldo possess sufficient cognitive capacities
to make a Will on February 25, 2014?

b)

Was Aldo subject to undue influence at the time
he made his Will?

4.

DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

4.1 Credibility

[
38
]

Given that Francesca’s version of Aldo’s
condition and of many relevant events is strikingly opposed to the one given by
Rina, and that the description of Aldo’s state by Rina is not compatible with
the information found in his medical record, the Court is compelled to commence
its analysis by addressing the issue of credibility.

[
39
]

Francesca’s testimony is corroborated by the
ones of Gianni, Mrs. Vidal and of Mrs. Gaudio
[15]
.
She describes Aldo, for all periods relevant to this matter, as a troubled,
suffering and diminished man. Rina’s version, that is somewhat corroborated by
the testimony of her son Nicholas, rather pictures Aldo as a “normal
individual”, “doing fine” and about whom no concern was to be had and this,
both prior and after his hospitalization from February 5 to 14, 2014,
continuing up to the end of April 2014.

[
40
]

Francesca’s testimony was nuanced, detailed and appeared
sincere. For example, she did not attempt to alter or temper the facts alleged
in her divorce application of May 28, 2014
[16]

regarding the nature and evolution of her relationship with Aldo, even though
these allegations indicate that they had ceased entertaining a loving
relationship since the mid-eighties, while continuing to live under the same
roof.

[
41
]

Francesca was able to provide plausible reasons
and explanations regarding events or situations, namely on the “cohabitation”
arrangement Aldo and her had agreed to when their marital relationship ended.
Francesca’s reasons and recital of events were also credible about the total
absence of relationship between Francesca’s family and that of Rina. Francesca
testified that the Iaccuci and Occhionero clans did not mix well, indeed almost
not at all, because Rina never accepted Aldo’s marriage to Francesca.

[
42
]

Rina’s credibility, on the other hand, is tainted
on several aspects.

[
43
]

Although she remained in a close relationship
with her brother Aldo through time, Rina was unable to give any reason why
herself and her children never saw or visited Aldo’s wife or children.

[
44
]

Like her son Nicholas, she pretended that Aldo
was “doing fine” from January 2014 up to April 28 or 29, 2014 when he entered a
coma like state in which he remained until his death a few days later on May 2,
2014.  According to her, Aldo “was the same man he had always been”, even after
his hospitalization and terminal cancer diagnosis.

[
45
]

Rina said that in February 2014, Aldo was
mobile, that they would dance together and take walks in the park near her
house, and that he was in the same shape and condition after his hospitalization.
However, Mike Occhionero (“
Mike
”) Rina’s other brother, testified that, after
his return from the hospital, Aldo would only put his coat on and take a few
steps in the yard behind Rina’s house.

[
46
]

Mike, who also lives with Rina, testified that
Aldo never complained about Francesca’s calls during the time he stayed at
Rina’s house.  This makes it difficult to believe Rina’s testimony that the content
of the letter sent to Francesca in mid-March 2014, truly represented Aldo’s
personal wishes or intentions.

[
47
]

Rina testified that she did not inform Gianni of
his father’s illness, because Aldo insisted that he wanted to tell Gianni
himself.  However, Gianni’s version is that it is Rina who warned him not to
call or to come to her house to see Aldo.

[
48
]

Although one might wonder why Gianni did not
take the matter any further to be able to see his father notwithstanding his
aunt’s threats, the Court believes Gianni’s version and concludes that Rina took
means to prevent any discussion or meeting to take place between Aldo and his
son, thus preventing Aldo from telling his son about his health condition.

[
49
]

Moreover, Mike testified that following his
release from the hospital, Aldo himself called Gianni and left him a voice
message, asking Gianni to call him back.

[
50
]

Finally, Rina testified that she only became aware
of the existence of the Will through the will search conducted after Aldo’s death.

[
51
]

However, Aldo’s social worker, Mrs.
Marie-Dalliah Jean-François, reported that, on March 21, 2014, Aldo mentioned in
Rina’s presence that his Will and Mandate were already made “excluding the wife”.
[17]

[
52
]

Mike also contradicted Rina’s version on her
“absence” knowledge of the Will.  He testified that in the days following
Aldo’s death, Rina told him about the Will.

[
53
]

For these reasons, the Court does not believe
Rina’s testimony.

4.2 The capacity to make a will

[
54
]

Capacity to make a will requires the testator to
have a sufficient memory, as well as comprehension and judgment skills to
understand the nature of the deed and its implications.

[
55
]

More particularly, in order to make a valid
will, the testator must:

-

Know, without being
prompted or helped, the nature and scope of the assets to be disposed of;

-

Know and understand the
nature of the deed that he is about to sign;

-

Remember the name and
identity of the beneficiaries in the Will;

-

Know the nature of his
relationship with the beneficiaries;

-

Understand and recall
all of these facts;

-

Be capable of
understanding the inter-relation between these factors;

-

Possess the capacity to
remember the decision taken.
[18]

[
56
]

In the present case, the medical staff did not
evaluate Aldo’s cognitive capacity using tests such as the MMSE or the MOCA.
[19]

[
57
]

Also, Aldo’s health consultations in the fall of
2013 for his ear and a tongue problems did not bring the physician to assess
his capacity.

[
58
]

It is not contested that prior to his last days,
and although these medications were prescribed to him after his release from
the hospital, Aldo did not use medication which could have directly impacted
his capacity.  It is therefore excluded that medication intake could have impaired
his capacity to make a will in February of 2014.

[
59
]

Nurse Caty and Dr Gaillardetz both testified
that they evaluated Aldo during their palliative care visits at Rina’s home.
They noted that he was “oriented” and answered questions appropriately.
However, they specified that the scope of the questionnaire they went over with
Aldo at each visit was simple.  It essentially related to his comfort level as
a home patient treated for terminal stage cancer.  They did not evaluate his
cognitive capacity and could not comment on same.

[
60
]

Dr. Jeffery Brock is the expert in demand.
Between 2000 and 2016, he worked with a senior clientele, dealing namely with
their cognitive impairment.
[20]

His expertise encompasses the screening of cognitive impairments through the
analysis of other symptoms.

[
61
]

In the case at bar, Dr Brock reviewed Aldo’s
medical files with Dr Marondo (consultation in September 2013), with Dr Abhoud
(ear-nose-throat specialist, October 2013) as well as his hospital chart at CH
Verdun (February 2014).

[
62
]

In his expertise report dated March 31, 2016, Dr
Brock expressed serious doubts as to whether Aldo was indeed capable to fully
and independently protect his civil and property rights on February 25, 2014.
[21]

[
63
]

Hearing the testimony of the other witnesses, which
provided additional information to assess Aldo’s capacity, Dr Brock reinforced
his position.  Thus, at the end of the trial, Dr Brock affirmed that Aldo
lacked sufficient capacity to make a valid Will on February 25, 2014.

[
64
]

At trial, Dr Brock testified that Rina’s
testimony regarding Aldo’s general and mental state at the time of the signing
of the Will, was not compatible with the medical notes in the CH Verdun file at
the time of his release on February 14.

[
65
]

In addition to the above, Dr Brock linked Aldo’s
abnormal gait to a sign of advanced dementia, and commented that it was highly
probable that Aldo suffered from moderate to severe dementia.  In this context,
Dr Brock projected that Aldo’s score at the MMSE, if administered, would have
fluctuated between 8 and 15
on his best days
.

[
66
]

According to the analytic chart for the
interpretation of the MMSE scores, with that kind of result, it would be
unlikely that Aldo would have had the capacity to make the Will.  A score
between 10 and 20 indicates a moderate psychometric impairment and a clear
impairment in the day to day activities, while a score between 0 and 10 reveals
a clear impairment and that the person is unlikely to be testable.

[22]

[
67
]

In any event, without referring to the MMSE
scale and strictly based on the medical evidence and the testimonies heard at
trial, Dr Brock opined that even if Aldo would have improved in the window of
time between his hospital release and the signing of the Will, such improvement
could not result in reinstating a sufficient capacity for Aldo to make a valid
will.

[
68
]

Rina did not produce any expertise to contradict
Dr. Brock’s analysis and conclusions, and there is no reason for the Court to
exclude Dr Brock’s professional opinion herein.

[
69
]

The proof in demand successfully sets aside the
presumption of capacity.

[
70
]

Here, given the medical evidence and the
testimonies, Aldo’s capacity can no longer be presumed.  Thus, in order for the
Court to conclude to the validity of the Will, Rina had the burden of
demonstrating that on February 25, 2014, Aldo possessed sufficient knowledge,
understanding and capacity to make a will.

[23]

[
71
]

Rina was not successful in making such
demonstration.

[
72
]

Nothing, aside from Rina’s testimony, indicated
that Aldo’s cognitive capacities had improved after February 11 and 12, 2014,
when it was observed by the medical staff that he was not oriented with respect
to space, time and persons,
[24]

that he required full assistance to get dressed and that it remained difficult
for him to understand instructions, even when told in Italian.
[25]

[
73
]

Mtre. Chartrand’s testimony was not helpful
either to show sufficient capacity, because the proof indicates that Mtre.
Chartrand did not attempt to verify it.  He declared that according to him, the
Will could be executed, because during his 10 to 15 minutes meeting with Aldo
for the signing of the Will, “nothing struck him” about the testator’s
condition.  However, Mtre. Chartrand at that time did not know of Aldo’s recent
health events and behavioral issues since the Fall of 2013.

4.3

The
undue influence

[
74
]

In the matter of
Gatti
vs.
Barbosa
,
the Superior Court explained that:

-

The burden of proof of
the undue influence lays with the party invoking it;

-

Undue influence is of
the nature of a fraud composed of reprehensible manoeuvers made with the objective
of orienting a person to grant a gift or a legacy which would otherwise not
have been granted;

-

The tribunal must be
convinced of the existence of such fraud and that it determined the testator’s
intentions in the contested will;

-

The situation must be
assessed globaly, taking into account the age of the testator, his state of
health, his social status and condition, his personality, the provisions of the
will, the isolation of the testator, denigration made by persons closed to him,
and the circumstances in which the contested will was executed;

-

Undue influence is
proven by oral or written proof, often by way of presumption.
[26]

[
75
]

Because a simple suspicion or hypothesis will
not suffice to establish undue influence, the factual situation of the case in
light of the proof provided must therefore be examined.

[
76
]

The medical notes at CH Verdun reveal that Rina,
sometimes joined by her brother Mike or one of her sons, was most of the time
present at Aldo’s bedside
[27]
,
while his wife and children were not even informed of his hospitalization.

[
77
]

On the eve of Aldo’s death, Rina falsely indicated
to the nurse that she did not want to inform Aldo’s children of his imminent
passing “because they would have been contacted three months ago and never
visited”.
[28]

[
78
]

The evidence as a whole demonstrates that in the
weeks that preceded the making of the Will as well as after it was signed, Rina
intentionally isolated her brother and manoeuvered to keep his wife and
children at distance, while at the same time, represented to Aldo that they had
abandoned him.  Rina also provided the medical staff and the social worker with
the same distorted version.

[
79
]

More specifically, the social worker’s notes of
her two meetings with Aldo on March 21 and 25
[29]
,
also attended by Rina, report a misleading and exaggerated charge against
Francesca, portraying her as a villain who expected nothing else than to
receive all of her husband’s money.  According to what the social worker was
told, Francesca was in denial of Aldo’s health issues, refused to care for him,
no longer wanted to have him in the house and would have dropped him at a metro
station for Rina to shelter him.

[
80
]

It was also suggested to the social worker that
Lisa had mental issues and drug problems, would have cut herself off from any
relationship with her family and that notwithstanding the invitations made,
Gianni refused to pay any visit to his father at Rina’s house.

[
81
]

At trial, Rina did not offer any reliable evidence
to substantiate or corroborate the situations or insinuations she reported to the
social worker about Francesca, Lisa or Gianni.

[
82
]

Thus, Rina’s allegations regarding Francesca’s,
Lisa’s and Gianni’s “bad behavior” or “lack of interest” regarding Aldo remain
what they are: false and misleading allegations, nothing more.

[
83
]

Although Ms. Dorothy Shestowsky testified to
support some of Rina’s allegations, Ms. Shestowsky’s testimony is not reliable.
The information on which she relied to testify had been told to her, for the
greater and relevant part of it, by Rina herself.  Given that the Court already
decided that Rina’s testimony is not credible, the same conclusion must apply
to Ms. Shetowsky’s testimony.

[
84
]

The Court finds that Rina denigrated her
brother’s wife and children without reservation and this, even to third
parties.  Excerpts of Aldo’s hospitalisation record at CH Verdun, where Aldo’s personal
history was given by Rina and noted in the medical chart
[30]
, convey in essence the same
version as the one she gave to the social worker.

[
85
]

Based on the social worker’s notes, the Court
can infer from the facts and circumstances that the “story” told by Rina to
third parties, in Aldo’s presence, subjected him to his sister’s undue
influence.

[
86
]

Although it may be surprising at first that
Francesca and Gianni did not insist more in trying to see Aldo or speak with
him while he was staying at Rina’s house, this first impression must be
modulated by taking into account that Aldo’s wife and children were not aware
of his true condition.

[
87
]

The Court does not ignore that since about 1985,
Francesca and Aldo were no longer entertaining a marital relationship within
the usual romantic or traditional meaning attached to such relationship.
However, they had agreed to stay together and to cohabitate.  This was the case
until Rina, on February 3, 2014, decided that Aldo would remain with her.

[
88
]

If Aldo really had the intention to make a will
to exclude his wife and children from his Estate, he could have done so over a
period of almost 30 years (1985 to 2014).  He never did, until Rina took the
matter in her own hands, at a moment when Aldo was sick, frail and vulnerable.

[
89
]

The Court is convinced that Rina exercised undue
influence on Aldo in order to bring him to make her the sole beneficiary under
his Will.

5.

CONCLUSION

[
90
]

Aldo’s Will must be annulled on both grounds:
lack of capacity and undue influence.

6
.
APPOINTMENT OF A LIQUIDATOR

[
91
]

Given Francesca’s acceptance, and considering
Lisa’s and Gianni’s consent that their mother act as liquidator to Aldo’s
Estate, the Court designates Francesca to act as liquidator.
